The following lines in commentary along with picturisation: (a) "as for example these specimens from the American radio in West Berlin." (b) "This man, slinking in and out among the tables, attracts attention. His billfold is much in evidence, he interrupts Conversations, and often has remarks to make. They are completely lacking in common sense or a sober approach. This gentleman and commonsense haven't been on speaking terms for a long time. The rancour within him breaks out in drunken yells. He is correspondent for the American Magazines "Life" and "Time". His gamois Lance Keeworth but he's known here as "Mr. Whiskey". "Life" and "Time" can be proud of their representative."

The following words together with picturisation of the small paper flags of the German Democratic Republic being burnt by lighted cigarettes and boys making holes in them: "With scornful smirks they wave flags of the German Democratic Republic after burning out the country's seal with lighted cigarettes. People remonstrate with them: Why have you done this? The insolent reply is: We're going to shoot through these holes."

The following: (a) "This sort of thing has occurred before.", together with the picturisation of Hitler patting the German soldiers. (b) "Boys like those were deceived by glowing promises, were called heroes, the saviour of Germany and Europe. Where are those boys today?" and the picturisation of the graveyard with crosses.
The words, "Yankee -- no."

The following: (a) "But in France too there are freshly-dug graves." (b) "This anti-war song was Outlawed in Paris," (c) "Daniel Ferri did not want to kill, and for that was himself killed," (d) "....and the O.A.S. murderers".

The following: "This is the stuff of which fascists are made. Among them may be potential murders. Their hate campaign never lets up. They must earn the money they've been handed....the whiskey they've been given. Unaccustomed to drinking, the youngsters quickly become intoxicated. The throats and derisive shouts begin all over again. It could be funny, were it not so despicable." "This idea from across the ocean has a damaged reputation."

The following: "Even today things are not quiet in Havana. Terrorists shoot from behind corners. They still blow up buildings. They are given weapons by people who don't want to see friendship between nations, between the people of Cuba and the United States......." "Quiet American".

The following: (a) "Expiate America's shame." (b) "I am surprised that the representative of the United States considers his own President to be a mythical figure.
